While we were receiving it from him, and his mouth was moist with it, a snake suddenly leapt, and we leapt at it to kill it, but it escaped. The Prophet ﷺ said: "You have been protected from its evil as it has been protected from your evil." From Kurayb, the client of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I recited Surat al-Mursalat, and Umm al-Fadl, the wife of al-'Abbas, heard me and wept, and said: "By Allah, my son, you have reminded me with this recitation of this surah. It is indeed the last thing I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in it during the Maghrib prayer." And Allah knows best. It has fifty verses.

﴿By those sent forth successively (1), then those that blow violently (2), and those that spread widely (3), then those that separate decisively (4), then those that deliver a reminder (5), as an excuse or a warning (6), indeed what you are promised will surely occur (7). So when the stars are obliterated (8), and when the sky is split open (9), and when the mountains are blown away (10), and when the messengers are brought to their appointed time (11), for what day has it been postponed (12)? For the Day of Decision (13). And what will make you know what the Day of Decision is? (14). Woe that Day to the deniers (15).﴾

The majority of the exegetes hold that ﴿those sent forth﴾ refers to the winds. Masruq related from 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) that he said: They are the angels, sent with what is known of Allah's command and prohibition, and of the news and the revelation. This is also the view of Abu Hurayrah, Muqatil, Abu Salih and al-Kalbi. It was also said: They are the prophets, who were sent with "There is no god but Allah," as said by Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Salih said: They are the messengers who are sent with the miracles by which they are recognised. And from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud: They are the winds, as Allah says: ﴿And We sent the winds﴾ [al-Hijr: 22], and He says: ﴿It is He who sends the winds﴾ [al-A'raf: 57].

The meaning of ʿurfan (successively) is that some of them follow others, like the mane (ʿurf) of a horse. The Arabs say: "The people came to so-and-so in one mane (ʿurf)," meaning when they turned to him in large numbers. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of "those sent forth," meaning: the winds that are sent in succession. It may also be a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning "in succession." It may also be that the accusative is by way of an implied preposition, as if he said: "those sent forth with ʿurf," and what is meant is the angels, or the angels and the messengers. It was also said: It is possible that what is meant by ﴿those sent forth﴾ is the clouds, because of what they contain of blessing and punishment, knowing what they were sent with and to whom they were sent. It was also said: They are the rebukes and admonitions. And ʿurfan according to this interpretation means "successive," like the mane of a horse, as said by Ibn Mas'ud. It was also said: "those that run," as said by al-Hasan, meaning in the hearts. And it was said: "those that are known" by the intellects.

﴿Then those that blow violently﴾: the winds, without disagreement, as said by al-Mahdawi. From Ibn Mas'ud: They are the violent winds that come with ʿaṣf, which is the leaves and debris of crops, as Allah says: ﴿then He sends against you a violent gale﴾ [al-Isra': 69]. It was also said: "Those that blow violently" are the angels entrusted with the winds, who drive them. It was also said: The angels seize the soul of the disbeliever. It is said: ʿaṣafa bi-l-shay'  meaning he annihilated and destroyed it, and a ʿaṣūd camel is one that throws its rider, so it goes on as if it were wind in its speed; and "the war swept (ʿaṣafat) the people," meaning it took them away. It was also said: It may be that they are the destroying signs, such as earthquakes and eclipses.

﴿And those that spread widely﴾: the angels entrusted with the clouds, who spread them. Ibn Mas'ud and Mujahid said: They are the winds, which Allah sends spreading before His mercy, meaning they spread the clouds for the rain. This was related from Abu Salih. And from him also: They are the rains, because they spread the plants, so nashr means revival; it is said: Allah "revived" (nashara) the dead and "brought him back to life" (anshara), meaning He gave him life. Al-Suddi related from him: They are the angels who spread the books of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He means what is spread of books and the deeds of the children of Adam. Al-Dahhak said: They are the scrolls spread before Allah with the deeds of the servants. Al-Rabi' said: It is the resurrection for the Day of Judgment, in which the souls are spread out. He said: ﴿and those that spread widely﴾ with the conjunction "wa," because it is the beginning of another oath.

﴿Then those that separate decisively﴾: the angels who descend with the separation between truth and falsehood, as said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Abu Salih. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "What the angels separate of provisions, sustenance and lifespans." Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid, who said: "Those that separate" are the winds, which separate the clouds and scatter them. From Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: ﴿those that separate decisively﴾ is the Furqan (the criterion), by which Allah separated truth from falsehood, and the lawful from the unlawful. This was also said by al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan. It was also said: It means the messengers, who separated between what Allah commanded and what He forbade, that is, they clarified that. It was also said: They are the rain-bearing clouds, by comparison with the she-camel that separates (fariq), which is the pregnant one that emerges and runs over the ground when she gives birth; and the plural is nūq fawāriq and furruq. And sometimes they liken a cloud that separates from the clouds to this she-camel. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"Or a cloud that separates, unveiling its flanks,
the flash of lightning opening it, and the darkness pitch-black."

[Tabawwuj al-barq: opening and uncovering it. ʿAlajum: intensely black.]

﴿Then those that deliver a reminder﴾: the angels, by consensus, meaning they deliver the books of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the prophets, peace be upon them, as said by al-Mahdawi. It was also said: It is Gabriel, and he was given the name of a plural because he used to descend with them. It was also said: The intended meaning is the messengers, who convey to their peoples what Allah revealed to them, as said by Qutrub. Ibn 'Abbas recited (fa-l-mulaqqiyat) with shaddah and a fatha on the qaf, and it is like Allah's saying: ﴿And indeed you are receiving the Qur'an﴾ [al-Naml: 6].

﴿as an excuse or a warning﴾: meaning they receive the revelation as an excuse from Allah, or as a warning to His creation of His punishment, as said by al-Farra'. From Abu Salih, who said: The messengers give excuse and give warning. Sa'id related from Qatadah, concerning ʿudhran: an excuse from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to His creation, and nudhran: a warning to the believers, so that they may benefit from it and act upon it. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: ʿudhran means what Allah, may His praise be exalted, delivers of the excuses of His allies, which is repentance; or nudhran means a warning to His enemies.

Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited ﴿or a warning﴾ (aw nudhran) with the dhal silent. All of the Seven read the dhal of ʿudhran silent, except what al-Ju'fi and al-A'sha related from Abu Bakr from 'Asim, that he vocalised the dhal. This was related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and others. Ibrahim al-Taymi and Qatadah read ʿudhran wa-nudhran with the conjunction "wa," and they did not put an alif between them. Both are accusative as objects of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning for the excuse or for the warning. It was also said: They are accusative as objects (maf'ul bihi). It was said: They are a substitution for dhikran, meaning "those that deliver ʿudhran or nudhran." Abu 'Ali said: It is possible that ʿudhr and nudhr, with the heavy form, are the plural of ʿadhir and nadhir, like His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the former warnings﴾ [al-Najm: 56]. So it is accusative as a circumstantial state of the delivering, meaning they deliver the reminder in the state of excuse and warning; or it is an object of dhikran, meaning those that deliver, that is, they mention an excuse or a warning. Al-Mubarrad said: Both in the heavy form are plurals, and the singular is ʿadhir and nadhir.

﴿Indeed what you are promised will surely occur﴾: this is the answer to the oath that precedes it, meaning what you are promised concerning the matter of the Resurrection will surely befall you and descend upon you.

Then He explained the time of its occurrence, saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾, meaning their light goes away and their brightness is erased, like the effacing of writing. It is said: "The thing was obliterated (ṭumisa)" when it was effaced, and it is "obliterated" (maṭmus). The wind obliterates traces, so the wind is "obliterating" (ṭamisah) and the trace is "obliterated" (ṭamisan), meaning maṭmus.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾: meaning it is opened and cleaved. From this is His saying: ﴿and the sky is opened, so it becomes gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19]. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is opened like a scroll is folded.

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾: meaning they are all taken away swiftly. It is said: "I blew the thing away (nasaftu al-shay') and uprooted it," when I take it all swiftly. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Kalbi used to say: They are levelled with the ground. The Arabs say: "A horse that is nasūf," when it pushes the girth back with its elbows; Bishr said:

"Nasūf for the girth with its two elbows."

And the she-camel "nasafat al-kala'" when she grazed it. Al-Mubarrad said: "nusifat" means they were uprooted from their place. A man says to a man who pulls his feet up from the ground: "Have your feet been blown away?" It was also said: Nasf is the scattering of the parts until the wind scatters them. From it: "the food was nusif," because it is shaken until the wind removes some of the chaff from it.

﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾: meaning they are gathered to their time for the Day of Resurrection. The "waqt" (time) is the ultimate limit at which the thing deferred to it is reached. So the meaning is: a time and a limit has been set for them for the judgment and the decision between them and the nations, as Allah says: ﴿On the Day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. It was also said: This is in this world, meaning the messengers were gathered at the time appointed for them, when the punishment would descend upon those who denied them, since the disbelievers are given respite. Doubts are only removed on the Day of Resurrection. The first view is better, because "appointing a time" (al-tawqit) means something that occurs on the Day of Resurrection, like the obliteration, the blowing away of the mountains, and the splitting of the sky, and it does not befit it to be set a time before the Day of Resurrection. Abu 'Ali said: That is, He made the Day of Religion and of Decision a time for them. It was also said: "uqqitat" means they were promised and given a term. It was also said: "uqqitat" means they were sent for known times, according to what Allah knew and willed. The hamzah in uqqitat is a substitution for the waw, as the author explained this substitution at His saying: ﴿Say: It has been revealed﴾ at the beginning of this part. This was said by al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra' said: Every waw that is given a damma, and whose damma is obligatory, may have a hamzah substituted for it. You say: "The people prayed in ones (uhdanan)," meaning wuhdanan, and they say: "These are fine faces (wujuh hisan) and ajuh" [a hamzah replacing the waw]. This is because the damma of the waw is heavy. And the substitution is not permitted in His saying: ﴿and do not forget kindness among yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237], because the damma there is not obligatory. Abu 'Amr, Humayd, al-Hasan and Nasr recited it, and from 'Asim and Mujahid: "wuqqitat" with a waw and a shaddah on the qaf, according to the original form. Abu 'Amr said: Only one who says "ajuh" for "wujuh" recites "uqqitat." Abu Ja'far, Shaybah and al-A'raj recited "wuqitat" with a waw and a lightened qaf. It is fu'ilat from al-waqt (time), and from it: ﴿a book prescribed at fixed times﴾ [al-Nisa': 103]. And from al-Hasan also: "wuwuqqitat" with two waws, which is fu'ilat from al-waqt also, like ʿuhidat. If the waw in these two readings were changed to an alif, it would be permissible. Yahya, Ayyub, Khalid ibn Ilyas and Salam recited "uqqitat" with a hamzah and lightening, because it is written in the Mushaf with an alif.

(For what day has it been deferred?) That is, postponed. This is an exaltation of that Day, so the question is one of glorification: it has been deferred until the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Fasl). Sa'id narrated from Qatadah, who said: "On it, people will be judged by their deeds, to Paradise or to Hell." It is also in a hadith: [When people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection, they will stand for forty years, the sun above their heads, their gazes fixed on the sky, awaiting the judgment [.

(And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?) After this glorification comes a further glorification: that is, "And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?"

(Woe on that Day to the deniers.) That is, punishment and disgrace for whoever denies Allah, His messengers, His books, and the Day of Judgment. This is a threat. He repeats it in this surah with every verse for those who deny, because He distributes it among them according to the degree of their denial. Each denier of something has a punishment in addition to his denial of something else, and there may be something he denied which is a greater sin than his denial of other things, because it is more shameful in his denial and greater in rejecting Allah. So the share of woe he receives is according to that degree, and according to the measure of his recompense, which is His words: "a fitting recompense" [al-Naba' 78:26]. It is narrated from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that he said: "Wayl is a valley in Hell containing various kinds of punishment." Ibn 'Abbas and others also said this. Ibn 'Abbas said: "When Hell subsides, some of its embers are taken and thrown back upon it, and some of it devours the rest." It is also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: [Hell was shown to me, and I did not see a valley greater than Wayl [. It is also narrated that it is the gathering place of what flows from the pus and discharge of the people of the Fire. Something flows only in the lowest parts of the earth where it splits open. The servants already know in this world that the worst places are those where filthy waters, impurities, and the washings of carrion and bathhouse water collect. So He mentioned that this valley is the pool of the discharge of the people of disbelief and polytheism, so that people of understanding would know that there is nothing more foul in its filth, more stinking in its stench, more bitter, or blacker than it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described it with what it contains of punishment, and that it is the greatest valley in Hell. Thus Allah the Exalted mentioned it in His threat in this surah.

The meaning of ʿurfan (successively) is that some of them follow others, like the mane (ʿurf) of a horse. The Arabs say: "The people came to so-and-so in one mane (ʿurf)," meaning when they turned to him in large numbers. [Tabawwuj al-barq: opening and uncovering it. ʿAlajum: intensely black.]

The wind obliterates traces, so the wind is "obliterating" (ṭamisah) and the trace is "obliterated" (ṭamisan), meaning maṭmus.

"Nasūf for the girth with its two elbows."

Yahya, Ayyub, Khalid ibn Ilyas and Salam recited "uqqitat" with a hamzah and lightening, because it is written in the Mushaf with an alif.

(For what day has it been deferred?) That is, postponed. This is an exaltation of that Day, so the question is one of glorification: it has been deferred until the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Fasl). (And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?) After this glorification comes a further glorification: that is, "And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?"

(Woe on that Day to the deniers.) That is, punishment and disgrace for whoever denies Allah, His messengers, His books, and the Day of Judgment. This is a threat. He repeats it in this surah with every verse for those who deny, because He distributes it among them according to the degree of their denial. Each denier of something has a punishment in addition to his denial of something else, and there may be something he denied which is a greater sin than his denial of other things, because it is more shameful in his denial and greater in rejecting Allah. So the share of woe he receives is according to that degree, and according to the measure of his recompense, which is His words: "a fitting recompense" [al-Naba' 78:26]. It is narrated from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that he said: "Wayl is a valley in Hell containing various kinds of punishment." Ibn 'Abbas and others also said this. Ibn 'Abbas said: "When Hell subsides, some of its embers are taken and thrown back upon it, and some of it devours the rest." It is also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: [Hell was shown to me, and I did not see a valley greater than Wayl [. It is also narrated that it is the gathering place of what flows from the pus and discharge of the people of the Fire. Something flows only in the lowest parts of the earth where it splits open. The servants already know in this world that the worst places are those where filthy waters, impurities, and the washings of carrion and bathhouse water collect. So He mentioned that this valley is the pool of the discharge of the people of disbelief and polytheism, so that people of understanding would know that there is nothing more foul in its filth, more stinking in its stench, more bitter, or blacker than it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described it with what it contains of punishment, and that it is the greatest valley in Hell. Thus Allah the Exalted mentioned it in His threat in this surah.

﴿And when the sky is split open﴾: meaning it is opened and cleaved. From this is His saying: ﴿and the sky is opened, so it becomes gates﴾ [al-Naba': 19]. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is opened like a scroll is folded.

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾: meaning they are all taken away swiftly. It is said: "I blew the thing away (nasaftu al-shay') and uprooted it," when I take it all swiftly. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Kalbi used to say: They are levelled with the ground. The Arabs say: "A horse that is nasūf," when it pushes the girth back with its elbows; Bishr said:

And the she-camel "nasafat al-kala'" when she grazed it. Al-Mubarrad said: "nusifat" means they were uprooted from their place. A man says to a man who pulls his feet up from the ground: "Have your feet been blown away?" It was also said: Nasf is the scattering of the parts until the wind scatters them. From it: "the food was nusif," because it is shaken until the wind removes some of the chaff from it.

﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾: meaning they are gathered to their time for the Day of Resurrection. The "waqt" (time) is the ultimate limit at which the thing deferred to it is reached. It was also said: This is in this world, meaning the messengers were gathered at the time appointed for them, when the punishment would descend upon those who denied them, since the disbelievers are given respite. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 77, verse 16–19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ He informs of the destruction of the disbelieving nations that passed away, from Adam until Muhammad ﷺ.

(Then We shall make the later ones follow them.) That is, We shall join the later ones to the former ones.

(Thus do We deal with the criminals.) That is, just as We did to those who came before, We shall do to the polytheists of Quraysh, either by the sword or by destruction. The majority of readers recited ﴿thumma nutbi'uhumu﴾ with a raised (nominative) vowel, as a new sentence (isti'naf). Al-A'raj recited ﴿nutbi'hum﴾ with a jussive (jazm), coordinated (ʿatf) upon ﴿Did We not destroy﴾, as you would say: "Did you not visit me, then I honour you?" The meaning is that He destroyed one people after another, according to the differing times of the messengers. Then He resumed with His saying, ﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾, meaning whoever will be destroyed afterwards. It is also possible that the sukun (quiescence) is a lightening of ﴿nutbi'uhum﴾ to avoid successive vowels. It is also narrated from him that the sukun was for lightening. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿thumma sanutbi'uhum﴾ (Then We shall surely make them follow), and the kaf in ﴿kadhalika﴾ (thus) is in the accusative position, meaning: We shall do the like of that destruction to every polytheist. Then it was said: its meaning is to make terrible the destruction of them in this world as a lesson (i'tibar). And it was said: it is a report of their punishment in the Hereafter.

(Then We shall make the later ones follow them.) That is, We shall join the later ones to the former ones.

(Thus do We deal with the criminals.) That is, just as We did to those who came before, We shall do to the polytheists of Quraysh, either by the sword or by destruction. The majority of readers recited ﴿thumma nutbi'uhumu﴾ with a raised (nominative) vowel, as a new sentence (isti'naf). Al-A'raj recited ﴿nutbi'hum﴾ with a jussive (jazm), coordinated (ʿatf) upon ﴿Did We not destroy﴾, as you would say: "Did you not visit me, then I honour you?" The meaning is that He destroyed one people after another, according to the differing times of the messengers. Then He resumed with His saying, ﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾, meaning whoever will be destroyed afterwards. It is also possible that the sukun (quiescence) is a lightening of ﴿nutbi'uhum﴾ to avoid successive vowels. It is also narrated from him that the sukun was for lightening. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿thumma sanutbi'uhum﴾ (Then We shall surely make them follow), and the kaf in ﴿kadhalika﴾ (thus) is in the accusative position, meaning: We shall do the like of that destruction to every polytheist. Then it was said: its meaning is to make terrible the destruction of them in this world as a lesson (i'tibar). And it was said: it is a report of their punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 77, verse 20–24:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ That is, weak and insignificant, and it is the sperm-drop (nutfah), which has already been discussed. This verse is a basis for the one who says that the creation of the embryo is from the man's water alone. The discussion of this has already passed.

(﴿Then We placed him in a secure lodging﴾) That is, in a safe place, which is the womb.

(﴿For a known term﴾) Mujahid said: until We shape him. It was also said: until the time of birth.

﴿Then We determined (fa-qadarna)﴾. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read (fa-qaddarna) with a doubled letter (tashdid), while the rest read it without doubling (takhfif), and both are two dialects with the same meaning. This was said by al-Kisa'i, al-Farra' and al-Qutabi. Al-Qutabi said: qadarna with the same meaning as the doubled qaddarna, just as you say qadartu kadha and qaddartuhu. From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ concerning the crescent moon: [If it is obscured for you, then determine for it (faqdurū lahu)], that is, determine for it the stages and the stations. Muhammad ibn al-Jahm related from al-Farra': "fa-qadarna," he said: and its doubling has been mentioned from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and its lightening. He said: It is not far that the meaning in doubling and lightening is one, because the Arabs say: qadara 'alayhi al-mawt and qaddara. Allah the Exalted said: "We have determined death among you" [al-Waqi'ah: 60], recited with lightening and doubling; and qadara 'alayhi rizqahu and qaddara. He said: Those who read it lightened argued, saying: if it were so, it would be "fa-ni'ma al-muqaddirun." Al-Farra' said: The Arabs combine both dialects. Allah the Exalted said: "So give respite to the disbelievers, give them respite gently" [al-Tariq: 17]. Al-A'sha said:

"She disowned me, and what she disowned was not of the events except the greying and the baldness."

It is related from Ikrimah: "fa-qadarna" lightened, from al-qudrah (power), and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, Abu Hatim and al-Kisa'i, due to His saying: "fa-ni'ma al-qadirun" (the most capable). As for the one who doubled it, it is from al-taqdir (determination), that is, "fa-qaddarna al-shaqiyya wa al-sa'id, fa-ni'ma al-muqaddirun." This was narrated by Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet ﷺ. It was also said: the meaning is "We determined him short or tall." Similar to this is from Ibn 'Abbas: "qaddarna mulkana" (We determined our kingdom). Al-Mahdawi said: This explanation is more fitting to the lightened recitation. I say: It is correct, for Ikrimah is the one who read "fa-qadarna" lightened, and he said: its meaning is "fa-malakna, fa-ni'ma al-malikun" (so We ruled, and how excellent are the rulers). Thus the two words give two different meanings: that We determined the time of birth and the states of the sperm-drop in its transition from one state to another until it became a complete human; or the wretched and the happy; or the tall and the short, all on the doubled reading. And it was said: they have the same meaning, as we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 77, verses 25–28:

There are two issues here. The first concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle?﴾, that is, gathering together: it gathers the living upon its back and the dead in its belly. This indicates the obligation of concealing the dead and burying them, and burying their hair and all else that is removed from them. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Trim your nails and bury your clippings" (and its explanation has passed in al-Baqarah [see vol. 2, p. 102]). It is said: kafattu al-shay'a akfituhu, meaning: when I gather it and draw it together. Al-kaft means gathering and collecting. Sibawayh recited:

"Noble when the snakes gather (tankafit) into their stones from the frost"

Abu 'Ubayd said: kifatan means containers. The jar (nihy) is called kift and kafit, because it holds the milk and gathers it. [Someone] said:

"You are today alive upon the earth, but tomorrow the earth will gather you (tadummuka) into a kifat."

Al-Sha'bi went out with a funeral and looked at the cemetery and said: "These are the receptacles of the dead." Then he looked at the houses and said: "These are the receptacles of the living."

The second [issue (the text does not give the wording of the second issue, and it is evident that this is its place, as is derived from Ibn al-'Arabi's Ahkam al-Quran)]: It is narrated from Rabi'ah concerning the grave-robber (nabbash) that he said: his hand is cut off. He was asked: "Why did you say that?" He said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?" So the earth is a protected place (hirz). This has passed in Surat al-Ma'idah [see vol. 6, p. 168]. They used to call Baqi' al-Gharqad a kaftah, because it is a graveyard that gathers the dead; the earth gathers the living to their dwellings and the dead to their graves. Also, the people's settling on the face of the earth, then their lying down upon it, is a gathering of them into it. It is said: it is a receptacle for the living, meaning the burial in the earth of what comes out of a person as waste, since there is no gathering in the way people are upon it, and gathering indicates enclosure from all aspects.

Al-Akhfash, Abu 'Ubaydah and Mujahid, in one of his two opinions, said: "the living and the dead" refer back to the earth, that is, the earth is divided into a living part, which produces growth, and a dead part, which does not produce growth.

Al-Farra' said: "living" and "dead" are in the accusative by the falling of "receptacle" upon them, meaning: Have We not made the earth a receptacle of living and dead? When they are given tanwin they are in the accusative, as in His saying: "or feeding on a day of hunger, an orphan" (al-Balad 14–15). It is also said: they are in the accusative as circumstantial states (hal) of the earth, meaning: from it such-and-such, and from it such-and-such.

Al-Akhfash said: kifatan is the plural of kafitah, and "the earth" is intended as a collective, so it is described with the plural.

Al-Khalil said: al-taktif is turning a thing over, back to belly or belly to back. It is said: inkafata al-qawm ila manazilihim, meaning they turned back. So the meaning of kifat is that they move about upon its back, turn back to it, and are buried in it.

﴿And We placed in it firm mountains﴾, that is, in the earth, ﴿lofty﴾ mountains. "Rawasi" means fixed ones, and "shamikhat" means tall ones; from this one says: shamakha bi-anfihi, when he raised it in pride. He said: ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water﴾, that is, We made for you watering. "Furat" is sweet water that is drunk and with which crops are irrigated. That is, We created the mountains and sent down sweet water. These matters are more wondrous than resurrection.

In some hadith, Abu Hurayrah said: "In the earth of Paradise there are the Euphrates, the Tigris, and the river Jordan." And in Sahih Muslim: "Sayhan and Jayhan, the Nile and the Euphrates, are all rivers of Paradise."

This is the day when they will not speak (﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾), meaning they will not talk. ﴿Nor will they be given permission, so that they may offer excuses﴾. That is, the Day of Resurrection has stages and appointed times, and this is one of the times in which they will not speak and will not be permitted to make excuses or disclaim their deeds.

It is narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Ibn al-Azraq asked him about the words of Allah, ﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾, and ﴿You will hear nothing but whispering﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:108), and Allah has also said, ﴿Some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾ (as-Saffat 37:27). He replied: Allah, mighty and majestic, says, ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ (al-Hajj 22:47). So each portion of these days has a different kind of these states.

It has also been said: they will not speak with a conclusive argument, and whoever speaks with what neither benefits nor avails is as though he had not spoken. Al-Hasan said: they will not speak with an argument, even though they will be speaking.

It has also been said that this is the time of their answer, ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:108), which has already been discussed (see vol. 12, p. 153).

Abu 'Uthman said: the vision of awe and the shame of sins silenced them.

Al-Junayd said: what excuse is there for one who turned away from his benefactor, denied him, and disbelieved his favours and blessings?

As for ﴿day﴾ being in the nominative (yawmu), this is the reading of the common reading (qira'at al-'amma), as an inchoative and predicate: that is, the angels say, "This is a day when they will not speak." It is also permissible that His words, ﴿Go forth﴾, are part of the angels' speech, and then Allah says to His friends, "This is a day when the disbelievers will not speak."

The meaning of "day" (al-yawm) is the hour and the time.

Yahya ibn Sultan narrated from Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, ﴿This is a day when they will not speak﴾ with the accusative (yawma). It is also narrated from Ibn Hurmuz and others. It is therefore permissible that it be indeclinable (mabni) because it is attached to a verb, and its position is nominative. This is the view of the Kufans (al-Kufiyyin). It is also permissible that it be in the accusative position, with the demonstrative referring to something other than the day. This is the view of the Basrans (al-Basriyyin), because according to them it is indeclinable only when it is attached to an indeclinable noun, and the verb here is declinable (mu'rab).

Al-Farra' said regarding the words of Allah, ﴿Nor will they be given permission, so that they may offer excuses﴾: the fa' (فَ) is a conjunction, meaning it is coordinated with "yu'dhanu" (they are given permission). This is permissible because the endings of the speech are with the nun (ـون). If he had said *fa-ya'taziru* (فَيَعْتَذِرُوا) it would not have matched the verse endings. He has also said, ﴿It shall not be decreed for them so that they die﴾ (Fatir 35:36) with the accusative, and all of it is correct. Similar is, ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him?﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:245), with both the accusative and the nominative.

It was also said: that is, you used to commit sins in the world, and now you are unable to do so, nor to defend yourselves. It was also said: it is a saying of the Prophet ﷺ, and it is then like the words of Hud: ﴿Plot against me, all of you, and give me no respite﴾ [Hud: 55].

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 77, verses 41–45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among shades and springs﴾. He informs of what the righteous will come to tomorrow. By "the shades" (zilal) is meant the shade of trees and the shade of palaces, in place of shade in the three branches (of shade mentioned in the surah). And in Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿They and their spouses will be in shade, reclining on couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56]. [[See vol. 15, p. 44.]]

(﴿And fruits of what they desire﴾) i.e., what they wish for. The common reading is "zilal" (ظِلالٍ). Al-A'raj, al-Zuhri and Talhah read "ẓulal" (ظُلَلٍ), the plural of ẓullah (ظُلَّة), meaning in Paradise. ﴿Eat and drink﴾, i.e., it will be said to them tomorrow: "This is in place of what is said to the polytheists: ﴿So if you have a plot, then plot against Me﴾." The phrase "eat and drink" is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the pronoun of "the righteous" in the adverbial phrase "among shades," meaning: they will be settled among shades, having that said to them.

(﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers﴾), i.e., We will reward those who did well in their belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in their deeds in this world.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 77, verse 48–50:

His Exalted saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down.﴾ That is, when it is said to these polytheists, "Bow down," meaning "Pray," they do not bow down, meaning they do not pray. This was said by Mujahid. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the Thaqif, who refused to pray, so this was revealed about them. Muqatil said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them, "Submit (aslimu)," and commanded them to pray, but they said, "We will not bow, for it is a disgrace upon us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: [There is no good in a religion that contains no bowing and no prostration.] It is mentioned that Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, entered the mosque after the afternoon prayer, and he was among those who did not consider bowing (ruku') permissible after the afternoon prayer. So he sat down and did not bow. A child said to him, "O shaykh, stand and bow." So he stood and bowed, and he did not argue with him based on what he held as his school of thought. He was asked about that, and he said: "I feared that I would be among those of whom it is said, 'And when it is said to them, bow down, they do not bow down.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: This is said to them in the Hereafter, when they are called to prostration but are unable to do so. Qatadah said: This refers to the world. Ibn al-'Arabi said: This verse is a proof for the obligation of bowing and for making it a pillar (rukn) of the prayer, and consensus has been established upon it. Some people thought that this applies only on the Day of Resurrection, and that it is not an abode of obligation, so no command would be directed there that would bring upon them woe and punishment. They are called to prostration only to expose the state of people in this world: whoever used to prostrate for Allah will be enabled to prostrate, and whoever used to prostrate to show off to others, his back will become one solid plate. It is also said: That is, when it is said to them, "Submit to the truth," they do not submit. So it is general to prayer and other things, and He mentioned prayer specifically because it is the foundation of the laws after monotheism. It is also said: the command is to faith, because prayer is not valid without faith.

His Exalted saying: ﴿So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ That is, if they do not affirm the Qur'an, which is the miracle and the proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger, peace be upon him, then in what will they believe? And it is repeated: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ for the sake of repeating the warning and the threat. It is also said: it is not a repetition, because by each statement He intended something different from what He intended by the other, as if He mentioned something and said, "Woe to whoever denies this," then mentioned something else and said, "Woe to whoever denies this," then mentioned something else and said, "Woe to whoever denies this." And so on to its end. The surah is concluded, and to Allah belongs all praise.
